curriculum.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS
curriculum.description: Introduce a specific topic using a clear introductory sentence paired with a simple definition. Focus: Defining a subject clearly at the start of an informative text. Examples: A mammal is an animal with fur, Sharks are fish that live in the ocean, The sun is a star that gives us light, An insect is a small bug with six legs, Seeds are what grow into plants, Clouds are made of water vapor, Planets move around the sun, Maps help us find places. Constraints: Use fill-in-the-blanks to complete topic introduction sentences.

status: authored; catalog-checked; each binding generator-probed once; not hydrated as a lesson; not runtime-tested
learnerAction: Write a first sentence that names the topic and says what kind of thing it is plus one feature ("A mammal is an animal with fur").

components.title: Meet a Topic Sentence
components.intent: Grade 2 informational paragraph about one animal or object. The model topic sentence must define the topic: name its category and one feature (A ___ is a ___ that ___). Child taps the topic sentence in the model, then writes their own with a frame.

components.title: Which Sentence Starts the Paragraph?
components.intent: Grade 2. Show a short informative paragraph with its first sentence missing. Options: one definition sentence (category + feature), one detail sentence from the body, one opinion, one off-topic sentence.

layout.title: Meet a Topic Sentence
layout.intent: Grade 2 informational paragraph about one animal or object. The model topic sentence must define the topic: name its category and one feature (A ___ is a ___ that ___). Child taps the topic sentence in the model, then writes their own with a frame.

layout.title: Which Sentence Starts the Paragraph?
layout.intent: Grade 2. Show a short informative paragraph with its first sentence missing. Options: one definition sentence (category + feature), one detail sentence from the body, one opinion, one off-topic sentence.

evidenceCriteria: Picks the defining sentence over a body detail (knowledge-check).
Writes "A/An [topic] is a [category] that/with [feature]" with a true category and feature. NOT currently judged by any primitive.
coverageLimits: paragraph-architect scores parts present, not quality: an empty frame counts as content (ParagraphArchitect.tsx:540-545, 693-697).
Its modes change only the prompt. Task and score are identical across informational, narrative and opinion.
The only scored right/wrong act is tapping the topic sentence in the model.

recommendation.rationale: Add a judged "define the topic" mode to paragraph-architect. The writing surface exists; what is missing is a check that the sentence names a category and a true feature. See brief 1.

curriculum.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS
curriculum.description: Draft a concluding statement that effectively brings the informative paragraph to a close. Focus: Creating a summary sentence that reinforces the topic without introducing new facts. Examples: Now you know about sharks, These are facts about insects, That is how seeds grow, This is why the sun is important, So clouds are very helpful, That is how maps work, Now you know all about planets, These are things to know about mammals. Constraints: Provide a body paragraph and offer three concluding options for the student to select the most appropriate one.

status: authored; catalog-checked; each binding generator-probed once; not hydrated as a lesson; not runtime-tested
learnerAction: Read a short body paragraph and choose (then write) a closing sentence that restates the topic without adding a new fact.

components.title: See How a Paragraph Ends
components.intent: Grade 2 informational paragraph. The model concluding sentence restates the topic with a closing phrase (Now you know..., That is how...) and adds no new fact.

components.title: Pick the Best Ending
components.intent: Grade 2. Show a 3-sentence informative paragraph. Options: one closing sentence that restates the topic; one that adds a NEW fact about the same topic; one that repeats only a single detail; one about a different topic.

components.title: Pick the Best Ending Again
components.intent: Grade 2, new topic. Same structure as before: restating close vs. new-fact sentence vs. single-detail sentence vs. off-topic.

layout.title: See How a Paragraph Ends

layout.intent: Grade 2, new topic. Same structure as before: restating close vs. new-fact sentence vs. single-detail sentence vs. off-topic.

evidenceCriteria: Chooses the restating close over a same-topic new-fact sentence on two fresh paragraphs.
Writing their own close is practiced in paragraph-architect but not scored.
coverageLimits: knowledge-check gives an honest choose-the-ending item (probe), but left alone it writes two off-topic distractors. The intent above asks for same-topic distractors; not re-probed.
Grade 2 has no length cap on the passage inset (prompt only).

recommendation.rationale: Reuse knowledge-check for the choice task the curriculum asks for. Writing a close is covered by brief 1 (same judged-sentence mode family).

curriculum.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS
curriculum.description: Students analyze words with affixes by identifying and attaching common prefixes and suffixes to base words. Focus: Decoding words using knowledge of prefixes (un-, re-, pre-) and suffixes (-ed, -ing, -ly). Examples: unhappy, rewrite, preview, jumped, playing, quickly, redo, dislike, walker, helpful. Constraints: Highlight the base word and affix in different colors in the word-builder.

evidenceCriteria: Says the target word from its meaning with the parts board visible (word-builder).
The objective says "attaching": the child never puts parts together; they only say the finished word.
coverageLimits: word-builder raises simple_affix to a grade 3 floor (gemini-word-builder.ts:197-199) and the workspace says grades 3-8, so the grade 2 vocabulary request is overridden (probe returned "Grade 3").
word-workout read_inflected is a code-owned list of 12 CVC words with -s/-ing/-ed. No prefixes and no -ly.
word-workout prints the whole curriculum objective as its title (probe).

recommendation.rationale: Give word-builder a grade 2 band and a build response: the child taps prefix/root/suffix cards to make the word for a meaning. This is the open-build modality (OB-3 already lists word-builder). See brief 3.

curriculum.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS
curriculum.description: Students analyze a read-aloud passage to extract the main idea or central message through systematic text evidence collection. Focus: Determining the overall point or central message of the narrative or text. Examples: The importance of kindness, the lesson learned by the protagonist, the significance of the invention, the moral of the fable, the primary topic of the report, why the animal adapted to its habitat, how weather affects the local ecosystem, the reason for the city festival. Constraints: The passage-studio must provide a short text segment where the student chooses the one best sentence that summarizes the entire passage from a list of distractors.

curriculum.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS
curriculum.description: Students listen to short audio passages and select the most important facts to summarize the core events. Focus: Identifying specific key details in informational and narrative text. Examples: The main goal of the scientist, the steps taken by the character, the final outcome of the experiment, the location of the event, the time period described, the reason for the character's choice, the central problem encountered, the solution reached. Constraints: The passage-studio will present a 100-word audio track followed by multiple-choice options to identify the top three key facts, ensuring all answers are directly supported by the text.

status: authored; catalog-checked; each binding generator-probed once; not hydrated as a lesson; not runtime-tested

evidenceCriteria: Says each blend word aloud from its tiles, judged against the target.
coverageLimits: As built, cvce_blend can never serve a blend: the generator pins the pattern to allowedTypes[0] = cvce (gemini-phonics-blender.ts:318). The probe got cake, bike, bone, cute, nine.
There are no final-blend examples in the prompt, and the UI never groups the blend apart from the vowel-consonant core.

recommendation.rationale: Fork the mode: split cvce_blend into cvce and blend (initial + final), the contract-first route for a mode that cannot serve half its name. Route to /eval-fix (PHB-1).
